intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor — front-line via RASolute 303 (NCT07491445)
expected_benefit: OS HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.30-0.53) vs chemotherapy in the RASolute 302 2L RAS-mutant PDAC trial (mOS 13.2 vs 6.7 mo, ORR 31.6% vs 11.2%); KRAS G12D sits inside the RAS G12 stratum that holds the effect (HR 0.40).
key_risks: grade >=3 rash 14% (most frequent grade >=3 TRAE; EGFR-inhibitor management applies)
grade >=3 stomatitis 12%
any-grade rash ~91% in the phase 1/2 PDAC set, driving ~48% dose-modification
grade >=3 TRAE 43.6% overall (below chemotherapy's 57.5% in the same trial)
preference_alignment: prefers_trials: YES (RASolute 303 recruiting, treatment-naive PDAC, accepts G12D). Oral, so no IV-chair burden — matches an unstated age-79 gentler-route lean. Neutral 0.5 weight; no toxicity veto to hit.
guideline_status: No NCCN consensus category (NCCN Pancreatic v2.2025 assigns none to any KRAS G12D agent); FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation; guideline-consonant as trial enrollment for an actionable driver.
rationale_summary: The board's rank-1 KRAS pick and the only feature-targeting option carrying a positive randomized phase 3 — four of five personas placed it first, all five endorsed it. RASolute 302 hit its OS endpoint at HR 0.40 in previously treated RAS-mutant PDAC, and the patient's G12D falls inside the ~92% RAS G12 stratum that holds that effect. Two honest limits keep it from being settled: the registration read is 2L while the patient is treatment-naive, so the front-line benefit rests on the unread RASolute 303; and the allele-specific estimate is borrowed from the G12 subgroup, not a pre-specified per-allele analysis. The risktaker's round-2 preference note grants that a captured toxicity-averse preference would push the gentler zoldonrasib up, since prefers_trials does not separate the two. No mechanism-level objection and no veto.
open_questions: Does the 2L OS benefit hold at first line in a treatment-naive 79-year-old (RASolute 303 unread)?
Is the G12D-specific benefit as strong as the pooled RAS G12 estimate?
Does tissue NGS confirm the plasma G12D call at enrollment-grade VAF?
likelihood_of_effect: High in 2L RAS G12 PDAC — OS HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.30-0.53), RASolute 302 (n=500); first-line benefit inferred from the unread RASolute 303.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (rash G3+ 14%, stomatitis G3+ 12%; G3+ TRAE 43.6% overall, below chemo)

counter_productive_moa.description: Mucocutaneous toxicity can force dose reductions that erode the exposure the survival signal depends on; no mechanism-level antagonism

overall: The only feature-targeting option with randomized phase 3 survival evidence; first-line benefit inferred from an unread trial and the allele estimate borrowed from a RAS G12 subgroup.

intervention_label: GFH375 / VS-7375, KRAS G12D(ON/OFF)-selective inhibitor + cetuximab — 1L cohort via NCT07644559
expected_benefit: Confirmed ORR 41% (90% CI 30-52) with 97% disease control in previously treated KRAS G12D PDAC at 600 mg (n=59 evaluable); mPFS 5.52 mo. Highest single-agent response on the patient's exact allele in the dossier.
key_risks: grade >=3 neutrophil decrease 8% (one grade 4 neutropenia)
grade >=3 anemia 8%
grade >=3 diarrhea 3% (any-grade diarrhea 56%); grade >=3 TRAE 30.3% overall
cetuximab partner in the 1L cohort adds acneiform rash, hypomagnesemia, and infusion reactions with no dedicated PDAC combination safety table
preference_alignment: prefers_trials: YES (NCT07644559 1L cohort recruiting, admits treatment-naive G12D PDAC at ECOG 1). Oral (+ IV cetuximab). Exact-allele match. Neutral 0.5 weight; no toxicity veto to hit.
guideline_status: No NCCN consensus category; guideline-consonant as trial enrollment. US sponsor (Verastem) 1L cohort with an ESMO 2025 (LBA84) presentation keeps it inside the Western-sponsored frame.
rationale_summary: A genuine allele match with the loudest single-agent response signal on the board (ORR 41%) and an open recruiting 1L cohort, so it lands the KRAS driver, prefers_trials, and the oral modality in one option — the risktaker and advocate led with it, and all five endorsed it. The critic and concensusite are honest that the 41% comes from a single-country (China) phase 1/2 with a 90% CI in a mostly >=2-prior-line population, so it ranks below the randomized daraxonrasib on evidence strength while tying it on agreement. The conservative and advocate both flag the cetuximab pairing as the uncharacterized layer: the drug's own cytopenia backbone is plannable, but the doublet's tolerability at 79 was never separately reported. No dissent that it belongs on the list, and no veto.
open_questions: Does the 41% 2L+ ORR translate to the treatment-naive 1L cohort?
How does the VS-7375 + cetuximab doublet tolerate in a 79-year-old (no combination safety table)?
Does the US 1L cohort's line/ECOG fit confirm on screening versus the China phase 1/2 base?
likelihood_of_effect: High allele-matched response — ORR 41% (90% CI 30-52), ESMO 2025 LBA84 (n=59), but single-country phase 1/2 and one line beyond the treatment-naive patient.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (neutropenia G3+ 8%, anemia G3+ 8%, diarrhea G3+ 3%; cetuximab rash/hypomagnesemia uncharacterized in combination)

counter_productive_moa.description: Cytopenias and cetuximab dermatologic toxicity can force dose reductions; no mechanism-level antagonism of the therapeutic goal

overall: The highest allele-matched single-agent response on the board with an open 1L slot, but the read is China-based, one line early, and the cetuximab doublet's tolerability at 79 is uncharacterized.

intervention_label: zoldonrasib (RMC-9805), KRAS G12D(ON)-selective inhibitor — front-line via RASolute 305 (NCT07621718)
expected_benefit: ORR 30% with 80% disease control in KRAS G12D PDAC at the exact allele (phase 1, n=40, 1200 mg/day); no CI reported and PFS/DoR immature.
key_risks: low-grade GI: nausea 27%, diarrhea 20%, vomiting 15%, rash 10% — almost all grade 1-2
grade 3 ALT rise 1%; no grade 4 or 5 treatment-related events
RASolute 305 chemo combination (mFOLFIRINOX or gem/nab-paclitaxel) has no published dedicated combination-toxicity table, so additive myelosuppression at 79 is unquantified
preference_alignment: prefers_trials: YES (RASolute 305 recruiting, requires KRAS G12D, treatment-naive PDAC). Oral. Exact-allele match with the cleanest tolerability in the set — the profile an age-79 toxicity-averse lean would reward. Neutral 0.5 weight.
guideline_status: No NCCN consensus category; guideline-consonant as trial enrollment. Registered double-blind front-line phase 3 (RASolute 305) is the strongest guideline-fit signal short of a readout.
rationale_summary: The allele-matched agent with the gentlest tolerability in the dossier — no grade 4/5 events, low-grade GI only — which the advocate reads as the pick to put in front of a 79-year-old. All five endorsed it; the critic and concensusite dissented on the position rather than the drug, since ranking an n=40 single-arm abstract above the randomized daraxonrasib inverts the one consensus survival signal. The conservative qualified the same way: the profile is genuinely clean, but durability is unmeasured and they will not co-sign ranking it first on safety alone. On a neutral 0.5 weight the randomized evidence keeps it behind daraxonrasib and behind GFH375's louder allele-matched ORR; a captured toxicity-averse preference would lift it. No veto.
open_questions: What is the durability (PFS/DoR not reported in the abstract)?
What is the additive myelosuppression when zoldonrasib is layered onto full-intensity chemo in RASolute 305 at 79?
Does the G12D-selective agent reproduce the preclinical FAS/CD8 immune reprogramming seen with the MRTX1133 tool compound at clinical exposures?
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate, allele-matched — ORR 30% / DCR 80% in G12D PDAC (phase 1, n=40, no CI; PFS/DoR immature). RASolute 305 will test it front-line.
toxicity_burden: Low (nausea 27%, diarrhea 20%, rash 10%; no G4/5 events at monotherapy dose)

counter_productive_moa.description: Critic and concensusite dissented on the thin single-arm base; durability unmeasured, so on-target activity may not translate to a durable effect

overall: The allele-matched, gentlest agent in the set — best tolerability for a 79-year-old, but the evidence is a single-arm n=40 abstract with no durability readout.

intervention_label: INCB161734, KRAS G12D-selective inhibitor + chemotherapy — front-line via DAWN-303 (NCT07522073)
expected_benefit: ORR 37% with 78% disease control in heavily pretreated KRAS G12D PDAC (phase 1 monotherapy, n=41, all >=2 prior lines); mPFS/mDoR not reached at ~5 months.
key_risks: grade >=3 neutropenia ~40% in the chemo-combination cohort — the construct the patient would actually enter
monotherapy GI toxicity 50-60% but grade 1-2, with rash and stomatitis notably absent
no treatment-related deaths; the ~40% neutropenia is synergistic marrow toxicity with no dedicated combination-safety characterization
parent phase 1 includes an anti-PD-1 (retifanlimab) cohort — low-yield given MSS/TMB 8.6 and not endorsed
preference_alignment: prefers_trials: YES (DAWN-303 recruiting, requires KRAS G12D, treatment-naive PDAC; phase 1 parent also enrolls at his line). Oral + IV chemotherapy. Second-sponsor allele match. Neutral 0.5 weight; no toxicity veto, but see the conservative dissent.
guideline_status: No NCCN consensus category; guideline-consonant as trial enrollment. Randomized double-blind chemo +/- INCB161734 front-line design.
rationale_summary: The strongest single-agent response number on the board (ORR 37%) with monotherapy GI toxicity that stays grade 1-2 and spares rash/stomatitis, which is why four personas ranked it. It drops to rank 4 because the enrollable front-line construct is the chemotherapy combination, and the conservative dissented in round 2 on the ~40% grade >=3 neutropenia that combination carries — synergistic marrow toxicity a neutral 0.5 weight does not shield a 79-year-old from. The critic and concensusite hold it at the same evidence grade as zoldonrasib (single-sponsor phase 1 abstract, immature PFS) and decline to reorder on the 37% versus 30% response gap, which the critic reads as within-noise. Above ceralasertib by a wide margin because it targets the lead driver directly. No veto.
open_questions: Is the late-line 37% ORR reproduced at first line (DAWN-303 unread)?
What is a manageable growth-factor/monitoring plan for the ~40% combination neutropenia at 79?
What is the durability (mPFS/mDoR immature at ~5 months)?
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate to high single-agent — ORR 37% / DCR 78% in pretreated G12D PDAC (phase 1, n=41, no CI; PFS not reached at ~5 mo). DAWN-303 tests it front-line.
toxicity_burden: High (combination-cohort G3+ neutropenia ~40%; monotherapy GI 50-60% grade 1-2)

counter_productive_moa.description: Conservative dissented on additive marrow toxicity: chemo-combination neutropenia can force dose reductions that erode delivered intensity at 79

overall: Strongest single-agent response number in the dossier, but the enrollable front-line construct bundles chemotherapy with ~40% grade >=3 neutropenia and no dedicated combination-safety data.

intervention_label: HRS-4642 (KRAS G12D inhibitor) + gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel — front-line via NCT07232875
expected_benefit: Confirmed ORR 63.3% (95% CI 43.9-80.1) in 30 treatment-naive KRAS G12D PDAC patients (phase 1b/2, HRS-4642 + gem/nab-paclitaxel) — the highest front-line response on the patient's exact allele and line; HRS-4642 monotherapy ORR was 20.8%, so most of the combination signal is chemo-attributable.
key_risks: grade >=3 TRAE 90.3% (mostly hematologic, gem/nab-paclitaxel-backbone-driven)
one treatment-related death (1/84) in the monotherapy safety set
HRS-4642 monotherapy metabolic signature: hypertriglyceridemia, hypercholesterolemia, neutropenia
IV route (not oral); the confirmatory phase 3 (NCT07232875) is not yet recruiting
preference_alignment: prefers_trials: PARTIAL (phase 3 NCT07232875 not yet recruiting, so the door is not currently open). IV, not oral. The 90.3% grade >=3 rate cuts hard against the age-79 toxicity-averse lean the free_text names, even though toxicity_vetoes is empty so no formal veto applies.
guideline_status: No NCCN consensus category; guideline-consonant as trial enrollment once recruiting. China-based (Jiangsu Hengrui) front-line program.
rationale_summary: The highest front-line response on the patient's exact allele (63.3% ORR) and an exact allele/tumor/line match, which is why the risktaker and critic kept it on their lists — but the board down-ranked it and it lands considered_with_caveats. Three of five (conservative, concensusite, advocate) dissented: the 90.3% grade >=3 TRAE rate plus one treatment-related death is a tolerability profile the conservative will not top-rank in a 79-year-old the free_text flags as likely more toxicity-averse than the neutral 0.5 weight encodes. The critic adds that the 63.3% is measured on a gem/nab-paclitaxel backbone with no control arm, so the effect is confounded — HRS-4642 monotherapy was only 20.8%. Evidence-integrity note carried honestly: the Nature Medicine paper has no PubMed record, so it is cited by DOI and the enrollable option is anchored on NCT07232875. No formal veto was issued (the conservative's objection was a dissent).
open_questions: How much of the 63.3% ORR is attributable to HRS-4642 versus the chemo backbone (monotherapy 20.8%)?
When does the confirmatory phase 3 (NCT07232875) open to enrollment?
Does the China-based safety/efficacy read transfer to a US 79-year-old?
likelihood_of_effect: High front-line response but confounded — ORR 63.3% (95% CI 43.9-80.1, n=30) on a chemo backbone; monotherapy contribution only ~20.8%.
toxicity_burden: High (grade >=3 TRAE 90.3%, mostly hematologic; one treatment-related death; hypertriglyceridemia/hypercholesterolemia signature)

counter_productive_moa.description: Backbone myelosuppression plus one treatment-related death can force intensity cuts that erode delivered benefit in an older marrow-limited patient

overall: The highest front-line ORR on the exact allele, but a 90.3% grade >=3 rate with a treatment-related death, an IV backbone, and a not-yet-recruiting phase 3 down-rank it against a toxicity-averse 79-year-old.

intervention_label: Pan-KRAS(ON) first-in-human inhibitors (BBO-11818, BLU-924, PF-07934040, LY3962673) — phase 1 baskets covering G12D
expected_benefit: No clinical efficacy readout. The only public signal is a sponsor update citing a single BBO-11818 PDAC partial response (56% shrinkage) with no denominator or ORR; the others are registry-stage with no data.
key_risks: no per-term grade >=3 safety table published for any of the four agents (empty toxicities across the dossier rows)
early monotherapy reads describe predominantly GI toxicity with no dose-limiting toxicities, but the safety base does not yet exist
most FIH baskets require >=1 prior line, so line-fit for a treatment-naive patient depends on the specific cohort
preference_alignment: prefers_trials: PARTIAL (recruiting baskets exist, but most enroll after standard therapy, so a treatment-naive patient may not fit the current cohort). Oral. On-axis (target KRAS G12D via pan-KRAS coverage). Neutral 0.5 weight.
guideline_status: No NCCN consensus category; investigational, pre-data. Not standard care.
rationale_summary: On-axis pan-KRAS agents that cover G12D but sit at tier 5 with no efficacy denominator, so no persona ranked them — the conservative and critic explicitly declined to rank a mechanism whose grade >=3 union rate does not yet exist. They are surfaced here as considered_with_caveats rather than dropped because they genuinely target the driver and have recruiting phase 1 slots; the honest read is that ranking them would be ranking novelty, not evidence. Grouped as one class row: BBO-11818 (KONQUER-101), BLU-924 (Blueprint/Sanofi), PF-07934040 (Pfizer), and LY3962673 (MOONRAY-01, Lilly). Low likelihood of a decision-grade benefit estimate until abstract-level readouts arrive (BBO-11818 expected 2H 2026). No dissent and no veto because the board attached no target row to a pre-data agent.
open_questions: When do abstract-level efficacy/safety readouts arrive for BBO-11818 and the others?
Which cohorts admit a treatment-naive patient versus requiring >=1 prior line?
Does any of these reproduce the G12D-selective response magnitude at clinical exposures?
likelihood_of_effect: Low / unquantified — no efficacy denominator; the only public signal is a single BBO-11818 PDAC partial response with no ORR (registry-stage class).
toxicity_burden: Low (none characterized — early reads describe predominantly grade 1-2 GI, no per-term G3+ table published)

counter_productive_moa.description: Pre-data mechanism with no plausible counter-productive vector established; the risk is absence of evidence, not a mechanistic antagonism

overall: On-axis pan-KRAS agents covering G12D with recruiting phase 1 slots, but no efficacy denominator exists yet, so they are a bank-for-later class rather than a present recommendation.

intervention_label: ceralasertib (AZD6738), ATR inhibitor (ARID1A synthetic-lethal axis) — via NCT03682289, gated on BAF250a IHC loss
expected_benefit: Confirmed ORR 14% (4/29) across all ARID1A-deficient tumors (phase 2 monotherapy); the 31% subset figure is gynecologic-histology only (endometrioid endometrial, ovarian clear cell) with no pancreatic responder shown.
key_risks: ATR-class cytopenias (anemia, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia); class anemia is dose-limiting (grade 3 anemia ~26-36% in related agents camonsertib and tuvusertib)
per-term grade >=3 rates not broken out in the abstract; only zero treatment-related deaths is reported
the unquantified ATR-class anemia burden is the specific safety gap at 79
preference_alignment: prefers_trials: PARTIAL (NCT03682289 is active-not-recruiting, so the door is currently closed). Oral, intermittent. Targets the secondary ARID1A axis. Neutral 0.5 weight; no toxicity veto.
guideline_status: No NCCN consensus category for an ARID1A/ATR agent in PDAC; germline-negative also closes the BRCA/PALB2 olaparib POLO maintenance route (NCCN category 2A).
rationale_summary: A mechanistically independent banked second axis off the ARID1A frameshift, ranked last by unanimous round-1 consensus — every persona placed it below all the KRAS agents. The synthesis formula scores it 0.6 because it drew no round-2 down-rank critiques (the board spent its critiques on the KRAS-agent ordering), but that is an artifact, not a signal it outranks HRS-4642 or the KRAS options; it is placed at the floor to match the board's actual placement. The evidence is honestly weak: no pancreatic responder exists in the ARID1A clinical data, activity concentrates in gynecologic histologies, and the preclinical ATR-ARID1A work was done in colorectal and ovarian models with no PDAC line. Entry gates on BAF250a IHC loss (only ~67% of ARID1A-mutant tumors show it), so the frameshift call alone does not confirm eligibility, and the lead basket is not recruiting. The EZH2 arm of this axis lost its lead agent when tazemetostat was withdrawn in March 2026. Considered_with_caveats: cross-tumor, IHC-gated, and not currently enrollable.
open_questions: Does BAF250a IHC confirm protein loss (frameshift predicts it only ~67% of the time)?
Does ATR inhibition engage basal-like PDAC at all (no PDAC responder in the clinical data)?
When does an ARID1A-stratified ATR basket re-open to enrollment?
likelihood_of_effect: Low for PDAC — confirmed ORR 14% across ARID1A-deficient tumors (PMID 41686845), activity concentrated in gynecologic histologies with zero pancreatic responders shown.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (ATR-class anemia / thrombocytopenia / neutropenia; per-term G3+ rates unreported, zero treatment-related deaths)

counter_productive_moa.description: Cross-tumor extrapolation with no PDAC responder; the synthetic-lethal effect may not engage basal-like PDAC, and class anemia limits exposure at 79

overall: A mechanistically independent banked second axis off the ARID1A frameshift, but no PDAC responder exists, entry is BAF250a-IHC-gated, and the lead basket is not recruiting.
